content.text: A firm-wide register of legal entities — every bank, fund, insurer, treasury and interdealer FCY faces — each identified by its LEI where one exists, modelled on the CDM

type. It serves every downstream consumer that must name a legal entity precisely: trade booking, master-agreement linkage, and regulatory counterparty classification. It exists now because the firm's standing rule R7 (FCY standing rules) requires every counterparty to be identified as a CDM
with an LEI, and no persisted register of legal entities exists in this deployment.
One register of legal entities, each realising the CDM
type: a required name and optional entity identifiers (LEI and other scheme-typed identifiers).
Uniqueness of the LEI across the register, and the LEI's 20-character alphanumeric format.
A lifecycle for records (draft / active / retired) so a defunct counterparty can be retired without losing its history.
The register's standard screens (search listing and edit form).
type and its party identifiers, roles, accounts and contact information — a separate, later concern; this spec covers only the legal entity itself.
records and the master-agreement stack — governed by standing rules R5/R6/R19 (FCY standing rules) but out of scope here.
GLEIF registry synchronisation or automated LEI verification against the public registry — the LEI is recorded as data, not verified live.
Trade booking and any screen beyond the register's own.
None — the register is a plain create/edit/browse surface; no ordered process crosses it.
R1: WHEN a legal entity is saved with an LEI that another record already carries, the system SHALL reject the save and name the conflicting record.
R2: WHILE a legal entity is retired, the system SHALL exclude it from selection for new business.
P1: A legal entity always has a name.

cells.text: The legal entity's name, as it appears on its governing documents.

unique when present; format(20 alphanumeric) — the Legal Entity Identifier, per FCY standing rule R7 (LEI in `Party.partyId` typed by `PartyIdentifierTypeEnum`); the register's flat `lei` field realises the CDM `EntityIdentifier` where `identifierType` is LEI.

content.text: (vocabulary, from the cdm corpus): a required name and an optional entity identifier such as the LEI. The CDM type carries

beans; this register narrows it to the one identifier FCY uses — the LEI — held flat, because the register's only consumer rule (FCY standing rule R7) keys on the LEI alone. If a second identifier scheme is ever needed, the field widens back to an embedded list without changing consumers.

Rules the table cannot carry: none — the LEI uniqueness, format and required name are all table rules; R2 (retired entities excluded from new business) is the one behavioural rule, and it binds consumers of the register, not the register itself.

The register's search screen and edit form — the platform's standard screens for the bean. No custom surface: a dense listing of legal entities filterable by status and searchable by name and LEI, with the edit form carrying the name, LEI and lifecycle status.

FCY standing rules R7 and R19 (from the company corpus, wiki/company/standing-rules.md) — R7 requires every counterparty to carry an LEI; R19 forbids booking against a counterparty with no in-force agreement, which is why the register carries a lifecycle a consumer can filter on.
Volume: ~40 active counterparties (company corpus, FCY counterparties) plus retired history — well within the platform's defaults; no performance target beyond them.
Considered, none apply: authorization (any signed-in user, the platform's default), availability, audit, privacy and retention, locale and time zones, cost.
A1 (verifies R1): the rejection of a save whose LEI is already carried by another record SHALL name that conflicting record.
A2 (verifies R2): WHILE a legal entity is in status retired, the system SHALL not offer it as a selectable counterparty for new business.
A3 (verifies P1): WHEN a legal entity is saved without a name, the system SHALL reject the save.
None — new entity, nothing to migrate. The register starts empty; counterparties are entered as they are onboarded.
A persisted LegalEntity register — one entity with its search screen and edit form.
Implied by the bean blocks in the Data model and regenerated by the platform - do not edit this block; author above it what the catalog cannot derive.

LegalEntity - persistence.entity (persistence): The entity class with its builder, its descriptor + jsontype entry, its migration and table, and its tests; the descriptor is authored at spec time as the bean's entity-descriptor attachment (entity_descriptors/{qualified-descriptor-name}.json).
LegalEntity - observer.sheet (observer): The observer sheet: the entity's only remote surface, reads and writes.

LegalEntity - ui.defaultForm (ui): The default form of one row, rendered wherever the row is viewed or edited: its layout JS, authored at spec time as the spec's ui/{qualified-descriptor-name}.js attachment and shipped beside the entity class.
